title.en: The writer, the war and the characters

hook.en: After a long war, a young woman returns to her town. Her mother is gone, her home is gone, and all she has left is an address someone once gave her.

objectives.en: Introduce Marga Minco and the background of the story
Identify the narrator, her mother and Mrs Dorling
Explain why the family's belongings were given away

narration.en: After a long war, a young woman returns to her town. Her mother is gone, her home is gone, and all she has left is an address someone once gave her.

body.en: Marga Minco is a Dutch writer from a Jewish family whose works return again and again to the Second World War and the persecution of Jews in the occupied Netherlands. "The Address" is a short story translated from Dutch. It is set just after the war, when survivors came back to find their homes and families destroyed.

points.en: Background: Nazi occupation of the Netherlands, World War II

narration.en: Marga Minco is a Dutch writer from a Jewish family whose works return again and again to the Second World War and the persecution of Jews in the occupied Netherlands. "The Address" is a short story translated from Dutch. It is set just after the war, when survivors came back to find their homes and families destroyed.
Let us map the people and things in this story around the narrator.

say.en: At the centre is the narrator, a young survivor returning after the war.
Her mother, Mrs S., did not survive the war.
Mrs Dorling, an old acquaintance, took the family's things for safekeeping.
Mrs Dorling's daughter later lets the narrator into the house.
The address is the narrator's only link to her old life.
And the objects themselves: tablecloth, silver, candle-holder.

body.en: The narrator is the daughter of a Jewish woman, referred to as Mrs S., who did not survive the war. Mrs Dorling, an old acquaintance of the mother, had offered during the war to keep the family's valuable things safe and carried many of them away. Mrs Dorling's teenage daughter appears briefly on the second visit.

points.en: Narrator: daughter of Mrs S., a war survivor
Mrs S.: the mother, who did not survive the war
Mrs Dorling: the acquaintance who took the belongings

Mrs Dorling, an old acquaintance of the mother, had offered during the war to keep the family's valuable things safe and carried many of them away. problem.en: Why did the narrator's mother give her belongings to Mrs Dorling?

steps.en: Context: a Jewish family in the Nazi-occupied Netherlands.
Danger: Jewish families were losing their homes and lives.
Mrs Dorling offered to keep the valuables safe until after the war.

answer.en: During the war the Jewish family was in grave danger and might lose everything. Mrs Dorling, an old acquaintance, offered to keep their valuable things safe, so the mother let her take them, hoping to recover them after the war.

points.en: Marga Minco writes about Jewish experience in the Netherlands during and after World War II.
The narrator returns after the war; her mother did not survive.
Mrs Dorling had taken the family's belongings, claiming to keep them safe.
